# Durability, Idempotency, and Recovery Checklist: Supervised Autonomous Loop

**Purpose**: Formal reviewer gate for durable state, effect, checkpoint, restart, replay, and
reconciliation requirements
**Created**: 2026-08-31
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md), [data model](../data-model.md), and [recovery quickstart](../quickstart.md#failure-and-recovery-exercises)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## State and Transaction Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are all Task, Execution, Approval, Project, and External Effect states accompanied by allowed transitions, terminal behavior, and authorized actors? [Completeness, Spec §Key Entities; Data Model §State transitions]
- [x] CHK002 Are domain-state, audit-event, idempotency-result, and outbox atomicity requirements explicit for every material command? [Clarity, Plan §Command and event path]
- [x] CHK003 Is `LISTEN`/notification behavior clearly a wakeup hint rather than durable delivery or canonical state? [Consistency, Research §R-003]
- [x] CHK004 Are optimistic versions, queue claims, lease expiry, and fencing tokens assigned distinct concurrency responsibilities? [Clarity, Data Model §Integrity and concurrency invariants]

## Idempotency and Effect Recovery

- [x] CHK005 Is an idempotency key defined from semantic intent and target rather than execution attempt or delivery ID? [Clarity, Spec §FR-023/FR-024]
- [x] CHK006 Are duplicate outcomes specified for project creation, delegation, approval decisions, controls, artifacts, audit identities, and effects? [Coverage, Spec §FR-024/SC-003]
- [x] CHK007 Does the crash matrix cover every boundary before intent, dispatch, mutation, result, commit, outbox publication, and browser acknowledgement? [Completeness, Quickstart §Failure and recovery exercises]
- [x] CHK008 Are `FAILED`, `UNKNOWN`, `RECONCILING`, and `RECONCILED` outcomes defined without equating reconciliation with success? [Clarity, Data Model §External effect transitions]
- [x] CHK009 Is blind retry explicitly prohibited when fixture ground truth remains indeterminate, with an actionable supervisor-blocked state? [Edge Case, Spec §US4 Scenario 5]
- [x] CHK010 Are stale fencing tokens required to fail even if a lost runtime later reconnects? [Coverage, Runner Contract §result outcomes]

## Checkpoint, Replay, and Restore

- [x] CHK011 Does the checkpoint requirement include every logical input needed to recover while making provider/harness session hints optional? [Completeness, Spec §FR-027/FR-029]
- [x] CHK012 Are corrupt, incompatible, task-mismatched, revision-mismatched, missing-artifact, and capability-gap checkpoints all assigned explicit outcomes? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases; Fake Contract §Checkpoint rules]
- [x] CHK013 Can cross-instance resume be measured against an uninterrupted deterministic artifact/evidence result without preserving runtime identity? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]
- [x] CHK014 Are SSE replay ordering, at-least-once delivery, duplicate suppression, and expired-cursor reset requirements mutually consistent? [Consistency, Plan §Command and event path; HTTP Contract §events]
- [x] CHK015 Are control-plane restart and full backup/restore specified as different recovery classes with distinct time and integrity criteria? [Clarity, Spec §SC-008; Plan §Migration, Backup, and Restore]
- [x] CHK016 Does the restore contract require scheduling to remain stopped until schema, manifest, artifact hashes, and projections validate? [Completeness, Quickstart §Backup and restore exercise]

## Notes

- Independent requirements review accepted all 16/16 items on 2026-08-31.
- A checked item approves the written recovery requirement, not a future crash-test result.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist state as a gate and must not modify markers.
